comparator.name: Astronomy
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations define a 150 EC Astronomy major and a 30 EC free minor. Astronomy and Astronomy Instrumentation and Informatics are optional deepening minors within that space. The regulations set the research-project entry requirements.
components: Introduction to Programming and Computational Methods
Take Introduction to Programming and Computational Methods first. The course includes an observing project with Groningen’s Gratama Telescope.
Builds on Calculus 1 and Linear Algebra.
Choose a 30 EC minor. Groningen offers optional deepening minors in Astronomy and in Astronomy Instrumentation and Informatics.
Normally requires 150 EC. Third-year Astronomy students who earn 135 EC within their first three years of registration may also start.

exception.reason: Groningen and Leiden both require observational astronomy, stellar and planetary physics and astronomical research. The accepted Groningen schedule teaches scientific computing, terrestrial imagery and robotics, but contains no sequence investigating stars, planets, galaxies or astronomical observations.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–2027 regulations define a 150 EC Astronomy major and a 30 EC free minor. Astronomy and Astronomy Instrumentation and Informatics are optional deepening minors within that space. The regulations set the research-project entry requirements.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The 24-course plan contains numerical mathematics, linear systems, statistics and image processing. UCR Earth observation interprets terrestrial and environmental data. Robotics develops sensors and motion planning. Neither course studies astronomical observation. The same absence of astronomical subjects persists in the feasible Leiden trial. Optional research cannot supply the missing sequence.

audience.programmeDescription: Astronomy at the University of Groningen uses physics, mathematics and observation to study planets, stars, galaxies and the matter between them. Students plan observations, analyse astronomical data and complete an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR teaches mathematical modelling, scientific computing and image analysis. Groningen applies these methods to stars, galaxies and planetary systems through observational astronomy, astrophysics and an astronomy research project.
